εὐ-σέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(εὐσεβής, which see), [in LXX: Pro.1.7, Isa.33.6 (יִרְאָה), Pro.13.11 (aliter in Heb.), Isa.11.2 (יְהוָֹה יִרְאָה), I Est.1.23, Wis.10.12, Sir.49.3, and very frequently in 4Mac ;] 
__1. piety, reverence (towards parents and others). 
__2. piety towards God, godliness: Act.3.12, 1Ti.2.2; 4.7-8; 6.5-6; 6.11, 2Pe.1.3; 1.6-7; τὸ τῆς εὐ. μυστήριον, 1Ti.3.16 ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ. διδασκαλία, 1Ti.6.3 ἡ ἀλήθεια ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ., Tit.1.1 μόρφωσις εὐσεβείας, 2Ti.3.5 pl. (see Bl., § 32, 6; Mayor on Jas.2.1), 2Pe.3.11 (on the use of εὐ. and cognates in Past. Epp., see CGT, on 1Ti.2.2 cf. also Cremer, 524).†
(AS)

Pirathon = "princely"
a town in Ephraim in the mount of the Amalekite
perhaps modern 'Ferata' located 1.5 miles (2.5 km) south from Jaffa on the road to Nablus
Also named: pir.a.to.ni (פִּרְעָתוֹנִי "Pirathon" H6553)

Pirathonite, of Pirathon "princely"

Another spelling of pir.a.ton (פִּרְעָתוֹן "Pirathon" H6552)
